title: C:motile-repair attempt (SIBRM): ringed swimming cells from noise (c28's ringswim-dl2) repair a 40% front cut against exact branched twins. 17 of 20 re-close their link ring within 100-140 steps and regrow; repaired cells swim on 3.7-4.1 body lengths with the ring held
summary: World: c28's ringswim-dl2, unchanged (phase-field cells with a self-made link ring, a phoretic drive, from smoothed noise everywhere; deterministic after init, so a branched twin is exact). At t=10000, on seeds 0, 1 and 3-8, twinrepair.py picks mature, compact, moving cells: one cell for 400 steps with no split or merge, aspect <= 1.5, area 0.6-1.6x the median, moved >= 0.5 R_eq. It branches an undamaged twin and deletes the 40% of the cell's pixels furthest along its motion (catalyst, links and phase set to 0: 44-53% of its links, 43-48% of its catalyst). On seeds 3-8 the wound keeps its substrate; on seeds 0-1 it is reset to bath (world.damage). Of 20 cut cells, 17 repair. Ring closure (share of the contour carrying links) goes from 0.30-0.72 just after the cut to >= 0.9 at +100-140, the cell regains its pre-cut area at +280-580, and its ring scores >= 1.5 in 100% of later frames. The 3 that die (+60 to +120) are exactly those left with closure <= 0.26 after the cut; every cell with >= 0.30 repaired. After repair, cut cells swim on: seed 6 cell 13, 3.71 body lengths (twin 3.61); seed 6 cell 8, 4.10 (twin 4.62); seed 8 cell 27, 3.86 (twin 1.46), each with the ring >= 1.5 throughout. Seed 8 cell 24's repaired cell converges onto its twin's configuration from +1200. Control: erasing only the links (shape and catalyst kept) kills 4/4 cells within 60-100 steps (seeds 0-1), so the cell's own link ring holds it up, and repair is the cell remaking it. Labkit packs with --damage 200:0.4:half on seeds 6 and 8 are in pack/.

claims.statement: In ringswim-dl2 runs from noise, mature ringed swimming cells cut by 40% at their front re-close their link ring (closure >= 0.9 by +100-140), regain their pre-cut area (+280-580) and swim on with the ring held, while their exact undamaged twins do the same uncut; 17 of 20 cuts on 8 seeds repair, and the 3 failures are the cells left with closure <= 0.26.
claims.track: seed 6, cell 13 (tr/s6_keepS_fig/twinrepair.png rows 1-2; table.txt): a 411 px ringed swimmer from noise, cut at t=10000 (40% of area, 49% of links), closure 0.30 -> >= 0.9 at +120, area back at +560, ring >= 1.5 in every later frame, swims 3.71 body lengths from +340 to +1900 (twin 3.61), then starts to divide

controls_run.R: an exact branched undamaged twin for each of the 20 cuts (tr/*/result.json, table.txt); wound substrate kept (seeds 3-8) vs reset to bath (seeds 0-1); links-only erasure, which is lethal 4/4 (tr/s0, tr/s1 ring rows)
controls_run.M: c28's mu=0 control (research/alife/collective/contrib/20261025T2209-c28-ringswim-sibmd-claim/README.md: no track swims 3 body lengths without the drive); here every twin is the matched uncut swimmer
controls_run.B: c28's chi=0 control (ring score median 1.11, 0% of frames >= 1.5); links-only erasure kills the cell (tr/s0, tr/s1)

claims.bd_control: not run for this claim (repair is the target, C:motile-repair is not diffusion-tested)

limits: Wall smoothing after the cut is curvature flow plus the link tilt (by construction, scored under mechanism), and the ring re-forms because links drift up the wall indicator (chi term, also built in). What the dynamics supply is the cell remaking enough links to hold its phase up before it collapses: below closure ~0.3 it does not. Cells in this world merge, divide and die within about 1000-2000 steps, so cut and twin diverge after the repair window like any two cells; the swim measure runs from +340 to the first split, merge or loss, and only 3 of 17 repaired cells keep a stretch long enough to reach 3 body lengths (others divide or merge first). Seeds 0-1 are c28's; 3-8 are new. Cells were chosen by a fixed rule, not by hand. 256^2 only; no resolution test.
